refactor(RingTheory/Ideal/Norm/AbsNorm): state the absNorm finiteness lemmas for rings with finite quotients (#45255)

Several lemmas about the absolute norm of an ideal exists in two copies: one for a finite `ℤ`-module, and a primed version for a ring with finite quotients, the first one being a restatement of the second. In this PR, the primed versions are kept, under the unprimed names, and the duplicates are deprecated. 

Three finiteness results that had no primed version but were restatements of lemmas in the `Ring.HasFiniteQuotients` namespace are deprecated in favor of those lemmas, and their uses updated. 

Note that the lemmas now require `Ring.HasFiniteQuotients R` rather than `Module.Finite ℤ R`. Where only the latter is available, the missing instance can be supplied by `Ring.HasFiniteQuotients.of_module_finite`.

The module docstring now advertises `Ring.HasFiniteQuotients.finite_cardQuot_le`, which is the result the finiteness statements rest on, rather than `finite_absNorm_le`, as suggested in #42790.

ci: post the batteries-pr-testing comment from its own job (#45356)

This PR moves the batteries-pr-testing status comment out of `test_lint` into a new `batteries_pr_comment` job, together with the `mathlib-nightly-testing` App token that posts it, to keep credentials out of the build and test jobs.

- `batteries_pr_comment` `needs: [build, test_lint]`, runs on `ubuntu-latest` with `contents: read`, checks out only this workflow's own local actions, and reads every build/test/lint outcome from the two jobs' outputs.
- It posts only when `test_lint` succeeded or failed. A run cancelled before `test_lint` starts records that job as `cancelled`, not `skipped`, so a looser condition would post a comment and reset the labels on every superseded run.
- The token is limited to `pull-requests: write`, which is all the labels and the comment need.
- The mathlib-ci checkout only provided the comment script, so it moves to the new job too, and `test_lint` no longer needs it.

ci: check the triggering run in `workflow_run` workflows (#45321)

This PR tightens the checks in the workflows triggered by `workflow_run`, so that they now also check the triggering run's event and repository.

`export_crossrefs.yml`, `nightly_detect_failure.yml` and `update_dependencies_zulip.yml` now act only on runs for pushes to this repository. `export_telemetry.yaml` also follows the fork CI, whose runs come from other repositories, so it accepts runs for `push` and `pull_request_target` events only, the two events our CI workflows use.

The concurrency groups of `export_crossrefs.yml` and `nightly_detect_failure.yml` now include the head repository. Runs that these workflows skip then never share a group with the real ones, so they can't cancel them.

`export_crossrefs.yml` also checks that the built commit is on the master **branch** and not a merely a tag named `master`. It is also split into 3 jobs, like `update_dependencies.yml` in #44881:
- `export` runs the Lean code with only `contents: read` and no cache access, and uploads `crossrefs.json` as an artifact.
- `publish` gets the `crossref-exports` environment and the app token, and runs no code from the checkout.
- `report_failure` posts the Zulip message when either job fails.

`update_dependencies_zulip.yml` now passes the `parse_changes` output to its scripts through `env` instead of writing it into the script text. `monitor-success` also gets the same repository check as `monitor-failures`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

ci: stop using the Actions cache (#45322)

This PR stops using the Actions cache in this repository, and adds a check to `actionlint.yml` that keeps it that way. Entries in the Actions cache saved by runs on the default branch potentially affect runs on every other ref that fall back to them. GitHub already stops runs of low-trust triggers such as `pull_request_target` from saving such entries, unless a workflow asks for `cache-mode: write`. But the two jobs that still restored from the cache open or push to pull requests, so it's simpler for them not to depend on it at all.

- `rm_set_option.yml` now uses an artifact instead. The restore step takes it only from earlier runs of this workflow on master started by the schedule or by hand, since pull requests can also start runs of this workflow file and upload artifacts from them.
- `lint_and_suggest_pr.yml` no longer caches pre-commit's hook environments, which only take a few seconds to set up anyways.
- `rm_set_option.yml`, the autofix job of `lint_and_suggest_pr.yml`, and the `report` job of `olean_report.yaml`, which handles PR content, set `cache-mode: none`. GitHub then refuses them any cache access, even from actions that use the cache internally.
- The new `no-actions-cache` job fails if anything under `.github/` uses `actions/cache`, turns on an action's `cache` input, uses `leanprover/lean-action` without `use-github-cache: false`, or asks for any `cache-mode` other than `read` or `none`.
- `.github/actionlint.yml` now also ignores the unknown `cache-mode` key in `.yaml` workflows, and `docs/workflows.md` mentions the new check.

feat(Algebra/QuadraticAlgebra): trace and norm lemmas (#45281)

Add some lemmas about the trace and the norm in `QuadraticAlgebra R a b`: the norm of `r • z` is `r ^ 2 * norm z`, and four times the norm of `z` is `trace z ^ 2 - discr a b * z.im ^ 2`. Also add that the discriminant of integer parameters is `0` or `1` modulo `4`, and a characterisation of `IsIntegralClosure A R B` when `A` acts faithfully on `B`.

These are used in a later PR to determine when `QuadraticAlgebra ℤ a b` is the integral closure of `ℤ` in `QuadraticAlgebra ℚ a b`.

feat(Topology/MetricSpace): a Gδ subset of a Polish space is Polish (#42693)

Adds `IsGδ.polishSpace`: a Gδ subset of a Polish space is Polish, which strengthens the existing IsOpen.polishSpace.

The proof follows the outline in Anush Tserunyan's descriptive set theory notes, https://www.math.mcgill.ca/atserunyan/Teaching_notes/dst_lectures.pdf where it is attributed to A. Bernshteyn. The "usual" approach (as in Kechris's Classical Descriptive Set Theory) constructs a complete compatible metric (the "Alexandrov metric"). The approach taken here is snappier to formalize - the idea is to give a closed embeddding from the G\delta set into another Polish space, and appeal to the fact closed subsets of Polish spaces are Polish. [Note the Alexandrov metric is recoverable from the embedding via the induced complete metrics on the product topology.]

feat(Topology/Connected): connected subsets of finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure (#41839)

This PR proves some properties of preconnected subsets of an extended metric space in terms of their Hausdorff measure.

- The extended diameter of a preconnected set is at most its one-dimensional Hausdorff measure
- A preconnected set with finite `d`-dimensional Hausdorff measure for some `d < 1` is a subsingleton, so any set with finite such measure is totally disconnected
- A preconnected set with finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure is totally bounded.

The main tool is that the distance from a fixed base point is `1`-Lipschitz (we define it by `x => (edist a x).toReal` and `ENNReal.toReal` is necessary because `ℝ≥0∞` is not an EMetric space and blocks me from using `LipschitzOnWith`, this is also the reason why I proved some weird lemmas like `isClopen_setOf_edist_ne_top` and `IsPreconnected.edist_ne_top`), so it does not increase Hausdorff measures, and the image of a preconnected set under it is an interval whose one-dimensional Hausdorff measure is its length. Comparing the two turns distances inside the set into lower bounds for its measure.

Some of these lemmas probably should belong to a different space. Feel free to give me some suggestions on this.

In the future, I would also like to use results in this PR to prove that a preconnected, compact subset with finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure is path-connected, and this is included in TODO.

Created with the help of Claude Code, carefully reviewed and golfed by myself.

Co-authored-by: Yongxi Lin <aaronlin@andrew.cmu.edu>

feat(Topology/Order): separability is hereditary for linearly ordered topological spaces (#41918)

In this PR we prove that
1. `isTopologicalBasis_isOpen_ordConnected`: in a linearly ordered topological space, every point of an open set `U` has an open `Set.OrdConnected` neighbourhood contained in `U`.
2. `countable_setOf_isolated_subtype`: in a separable linearly ordered topological space, the points of a subset `s` that are isolated in the subspace `s` form a countable set.
3. A subset of a separable linearly ordered topological space is separable in the subspace topology. This is proved as an instance.

The material was developed for showing the measurability of the pathwise variation of a continuous stochastic process in https://github.com/RemyDegenne/brownian-motion/pull/494. Created with the help of Claude Code, carefully reviewed and golfed by myself.

Co-authored-by: Yongxi Lin <aaronlin@andrew.cmu.edu>

ci: skip the inputRev check on bump branches and PRs into them (#45382)

`bump/*` branches now live in `mathlib4` rather than `mathlib4-nightly-testing`. PRs into them, such as the `downstream-lean4` export in #45345, depend on the `nightly-testing` branches of our dependencies. The "validate lake-manifest.json inputRevs" step in `build_template.yml` runs on these branches and fails them, though it used to be skipped when the branches were in the nightly-testing repo.

This PR skips the validation step when either of these starts with `bump/`:
- `github.ref_name`: pushes to `bump/*` branches, including the automation's `bump/nightly-*` branches.
- `github.base_ref`: PRs into a `bump/*` branch, from any repo.
(Note that `head_ref` is not read, so a PR from a branch starting with `bump/` can't get around this.)

Not covered: a non-`bump/*` branch pushed to mathlib4 with a PR into a bump branch. Push builds can't see the PR's base, so the check still runs there. (No one should be creating such branches and we have branch protection rules against this.)

feat(Analysis/Calculus): parametric integrals over smooth functions are smooth (#31141)

Show that for any smooth function `f : H × ℝ → E`, the parametric integral `fun x ↦ ∫ t in a..b, f (x, t) ∂μ` is smooth too.

The argument proceeds inductively, using the fact that derivatives of parametric integrals can themselves be computed as parametric integrals. The necessary lemmas on derivatives of parametric integrals already existed, but took some work to apply due to their generality; we state some convenient special cases.

chore: replace `irreducible_def` with `no_expose` (#45063)

The `no_expose` attribute can be used in place of `irreducible_def`, and leads to easier proofs because the definition can be unfolded the file containing the definition.

Another difference is that by using `no_expose`, the definition value is not exported at all, so in downstream modules it cannot be unfolded with e.g. `rw [foo]` or `rw [foo_def]`. Instead, a public lemma like `foo_def` needs to be added explicitly. This PR does that where necessary. If there is no such lemma, but you still need access to the definition value, `import all` can be used as a workaround.

Since mathlib now enforces downstream users to use the `module` system, we don't need to worry about downstream users that don't see the effects of `no_expose`.

Make the `choice` field of `Setoid.gi` actually have the correct defeq, which is the entire point of the `choice` field, instead of just using `EqvGen.setoid`.

chore: fix mergewithgrind exceptions (#45037)

This fixes the warnings from the `mergeWithGrind` linter, as reported [here]([#mathlib4 > Weekly linting log @ 💬](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/287929-mathlib4/topic/Weekly.20linting.20log/near/632946433)) by @SnirBroshi.

Some files become a bit slower, see radar output below, but nothing significant IMO.

Co-authored-by: Batixx <s59fpern@uni-bonn.de>
feat(Analysis/Gamma): bound `‖Gamma s‖ ≤ ‖Gamma (s + n)‖` (#45103)

chore(Analysis/Normed/Ring/WithAbs): avoid instance diamond at implicit transparency (#45144)

Found by the linter in #38781.

Co-authored-by: Jovan Gerbscheid <jovan.gerbscheid@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: grunweg <10105016+grunweg@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Monica Omar <23701951+themathqueen@users.noreply.github.com>

feat(Data/Nat/Prime): add divisibility lemma and golf proof (#45283)

Add `Nat.exists_prime_dvd_and_dvd_div`: if `m ∣ n` and `m ≠ n`, then there is a prime number `p ∣ n` such that `m ∣ n / p`. This is used to golf the proof of `orderOf_eq_of_pow_and_pow_div_prime` and to remove the unnecessary hypothesis `hn : 0 < n`. Two callers are updated accordingly.  The file `OrderOfElement.lean` is now under 1500 lines, so the `longFile` linter override is removed. 

I used Claude to help me debug the initial CI failure (`longFile` linter being the culprit) and I also incorporated some golfing suggestions made by it.

chore(Order/OmegaCompletePartialOrder): automated extraction from #44363 (#45299)

This PR was automatically created from PR #44363 by @Parcly-Taxel via a [review comment](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/44363#discussion_r4375032856) by @grunweg.

Co-authored-by: Parcly-Taxel <54175463+Parcly-Taxel@users.noreply.github.com>

refactor(RingTheory/Ideal): deprecate Ideal.mul_eq_inf_of_coprime (#44634)

Deprecate `Ideal.mul_eq_inf_of_coprime` in favor of `Ideal.mul_eq_inf_of_isCoprime`, resolving the TODO in `Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Operations.lean`.

feat(Algebra/CharP/Subring): generalize (#44918)

Generalize some instances from concrete subfoos to arbitrary `SubsemiringClass`, and provide an instance `SubsemiringClass.expChar`.

feat(Data/Finsupp/Defs): `(g.mapRange f hf).support = g.support` if `f x = 0 → x = 0` (#45201)

It is a lemma used in #45208.

perf(Tactic/Echelon): allow any type for computations (#45233)

This PR refactors the ring computations in the bareiss decomposition algorithm to allow using any type for the computations. Previously, it could only be `Expr` or `Int`.

A natural way to allow this is to make the carrier type `V` a field of the `Model` structure. Unfortunately, this puts it in `Type 1`, which means it cannot be passed through `IO`/`MetaM`. Instead, we use an approach based on `unsafeCast`. The same approach is used in different places in Lean core, such as to handle environment extensions (which need to store arbitrary types), https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/blob/v4.36.0-rc1/src/Lean/Meta/Tactic/Grind/Types.lean#L118-L121 and https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/blob/v4.36.0-rc1/src/Lean/Meta/Sym/SymM.lean#L31-L34 ..

doc(Topology/Order/LocalExtr): fix typos and outdated references (#45243)

Maintain the docstrings in `Order/Filter/Extr` and `Topology/Order/LocalExtr`

chore(LinearAlgebra/Countable): remove Finsupp namespace (#45259)

`Countable.of_moduleFinite` and `Uncountable.of_moduleFinite` do not belong in the `Finsupp` namespace.

fix(Tactic/ComputeDegree): fix `compute_degree` for polynomials with negated subterms (#45303)

Previously `compute_degree` did not recurse into negated subterms so `compute_degree!` would fail on:

    natDegree (-1 + X : ℤ[X]) = 1

with an unsolved goal error:

    ¬-(coeff 1) 1 + 1 = 0

This PR adds `coeff_neg_of_eq`, similar to `coeff_sub_of_eq`, and uses it when dispatching on `Neg.neg` when processing polynomial `Expr` which adds a hypothesis so the tactic can recurse.

feat: normal functions are (left) order continuous (#44954)

This is just a first pass, and I suspect the APIs can be unified further.
feat(Algebra/Order): `Additive M` is order-isomorphic to `M` (#45269)

feat(OmegaCompletePartialOrder): missing dsimp lemmas for Pi (#45339)

This also replaces the `simps` lemmas for `Prod` with manual lemmas, to make the names match `Prod.fst_sup` and `Prod.snd_sup`.

We drop `protected def ωSupImpl (c : Chain (α × β)) : α × β :=` without deprecation, as there was never any reason to use it over `ωSup`.

+  # on the default branch saved, and the jobs that used to restore from it opened or pushed to
+  # pull requests. Rather than vet every job that can save entries, we don't use the cache at
+  # all. GitHub already stops runs of low-trust triggers such as `pull_request_target` from

+  # This job checks that nothing uses the cache, and that nothing asks for more than
+  # `cache-mode: read`.
+  no-actions-cache:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout
+        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
+
+      - name: Check that nothing uses the Actions cache
+        run: |
+          status=0
+          # `actions/cache`, and its `restore` and `save` actions.
+          if grep -rnE '^\s*(-\s+)?uses:\s*["'\'']?actions/cache(/|@)' .github; then
+            echo "::error::Don't use actions/cache: see the comment on the no-actions-cache job."
+            status=1
+          fi
+          # The `cache` input of actions/setup-python, actions/setup-node and the like.
+          if grep -rnE '^\s*cache:' .github |
+              grep -vE '^[^:]+:[0-9]+:\s*cache:\s*["'\'']?false["'\'']?\s*(#.*)?$'; then
+            echo "::error::Don't turn on an action's caching: see the comment on the no-actions-cache job."
+            status=1
+          fi
+          # `cache-mode: write` or `write-only` would let low-trust triggers save entries again.
+          if grep -rnE '^\s*cache-mode:' .github |
+              grep -vE '^[^:]+:[0-9]+:\s*cache-mode:\s*["'\'']?(read|none)["'\'']?\s*(#.*)?$'; then
+            echo "::error::Only \`cache-mode: read\` and \`cache-mode: none\` are allowed: see the comment on the no-actions-cache job."
+            status=1
+          fi
+          # leanprover/lean-action uses the Actions cache unless `use-github-cache` is false.
+          while IFS= read -r f; do
+            uses=$(grep -cE 'uses:\s*["'\'']?leanprover/lean-action@' "${f}")
+            off=$(grep -cE '^\s*use-github-cache:\s*["'\'']?false["'\'']?\s*(#.*)?$' "${f}")

+# Area of a triangle
+
+This file collects formulas for the area of a triangle and other related results.
+
+## Main theorems
+
+* `Affine.Triangle.volume_eq_height_mul`: $S = \frac{1}{2}hb$

+  let e : Fin 3 ≃ Fin 3 := List.Nodup.getEquivOfForallMemList [i₁, i₂, i₃] (by grind) (by grind)

+include h₁₂ h₁₃ h₂₃ in

+    t.volume = 2⁻¹ * dist (t.points i₁) (t.points i₂) * dist (t.points i₂) (t.points i₃) *
+      Real.sin (∠ (t.points i₁) (t.points i₂) (t.points i₃)) := by
+  rw [t.volume_eq_height_mul h₁₂ h₁₃ h₂₃, t.height_eq_sin_mul_dist h₁₂ h₁₃ h₂₃]

+module
+
+public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Dimension.Finrank
+public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Algebraic.Basic
+
+import Mathlib.RingTheory.Algebraic.Integral
+
+/-!
+# Rank theorems over domains
+
+This file proves some `Module.rank` and `Module.finrank` theorems for modules over domains.
+
+## Main results
+
+Let `M/S/R` be a tower where `R`, `S` are domains.
+
+We obtain the following tower laws:
+- `Module.rank_mul_rank_of_isFractionRing_isLocalization` & variants: when `(R⁰)⁻¹ S = (S⁰)⁻¹ S`.
+- `Module.rank_mul_rank_of_field_isLocalization` & variants:
+  wrapper for the above that only asks `(R⁰)⁻¹ S` to be a field.
+- `Module.IsTorsionFree.erank_mul_erank`, `Module.IsTorsionFree.finrank_mul_finrank`:
+  when `M` is torsion-free over `S`. We only get truncated cardinalities.
+- `Algebra.IsAlgebraic.rank_mul_rank` & variants: when `S/R` is algebraic.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+universe v w
+
+open Algebra Cardinal Module
+open Module (rank)
+open scoped nonZeroDivisors
+
+variable (R : Type*) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [NoZeroDivisors S] [Algebra R S]
+
+namespace Module
+
+private lemma lift_rank_mul_lift_rank_of_isFractionRing_localization
+    [IsFractionRing S (Localization (algebraMapSubmonoid S R⁰))]
+    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M] :
+    lift.{w} (rank R S) * lift.{v} (rank S M) = lift.{v} (rank R M) := by
+  by_cases h : FaithfulSMul R S
+  case neg =>
+    have : ¬ FaithfulSMul R M := mt (·.tower_bot ..) h
+    simp [rank_eq_zero_of_not_faithfulSMul, h, this]
+  nontriviality R using subsingleton R S
+  have : NoZeroDivisors R := .of_faithfulSMul R S
+  have : Nontrivial S := FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective R S |>.nontrivial
+  have : IsDomain S := {}
+  let FR := FractionRing R
+  let mS := algebraMapSubmonoid S R⁰
+  let FS := Localization mS
+  let M' := LocalizedModule mS M
+  let : Field FS := IsFractionRing.toField S
+  let f : M →ₗ[S] M' := LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap ..
+  let : Module FR M' := .restrictScalars _ FS M'
+  have : IsScalarTower FR FS M' := .restrictScalars ..
+  have : IsScalarTower R FR M' := .to₁₂₄ (P := FS) ..
+  have h₀ := IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange R⁰ FR (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R S FS).toLinearMap
+  have h₁ := IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange mS FS f |>.lift_rank_eq
+  have h₂ := IsLocalizedModule.restrictScalars R⁰ f |>.isBaseChange R⁰ FR |>.lift_rank_eq
+  rw [lift_id'.{w, v}, lift_umax] at h₁ h₂
+  rw [← h₁, ← h₂, ← lift_inj.{_, v}, lift_mul, ← lift_rank_mul_lift_rank FR FS M',
+    ← lift_lift.{v, w}, h₀.lift_rank_eq, lift_lift, lift_lift]
+
+section isFractionRing_isLocalization
+
+variable
+  (FS : Type*) [CommRing FS] [Algebra S FS] [IsFractionRing S FS]
+  [h : IsLocalization (algebraMapSubmonoid S R⁰) FS]
+  (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
+  (M₁ : Type v) [AddCommGroup M₁] [Module R M₁] [Module S M₁] [IsScalarTower R S M₁]
+include h
+
+/-- **Tower law over domains.**
+When `M` is a module over an algebra `S/R` of domains such that `(R⁰)⁻¹ S = (S⁰)⁻¹ S`,
+we obtain a tower law.
+
+See `_root.lift_rank_mul_lift_rank` for when your modules are free.
+-/
+theorem lift_rank_mul_lift_rank_of_isFractionRing_isLocalization :
+    lift.{w} (rank R S) * lift.{v} (rank S M) = lift.{v} (rank R M) :=
+  have : IsFractionRing S (Localization (algebraMapSubmonoid S R⁰)) :=
+    .of_algEquiv <| IsLocalization.algEquiv (algebraMapSubmonoid S R⁰) FS _
+  lift_rank_mul_lift_rank_of_isFractionRing_localization ..
+
+/-- **Tower law over domains.**
+When `M` is a module over an algebra `S/R` of domains such that `(R⁰)⁻¹ S = (S⁰)⁻¹ S`,
+we obtain a tower law.
+
+See `_root.rank_mul_rank` for when your modules are free.
+-/
+theorem rank_mul_rank_of_isFractionRing_isLocalization :
+    rank R S * rank S M₁ = rank R M₁ := by
+  simpa using lift_rank_mul_lift_rank_of_isFractionRing_isLocalization R S FS M₁
+
+/-- **Tower law over domains.**
+When `M` is a module over an algebra `S/R` of domains such that `(R⁰)⁻¹ S = (S⁰)⁻¹ S`,
+we obtain a tower law.
+
+See `Module.finrank_mul_finrank` for when your modules are free.
+-/
+theorem finrank_mul_finrank_of_isFractionRing_isLocalization :
+    finrank R S * finrank S M = finrank R M := by
+  simpa [finrank] using
+    congr(toNat $(lift_rank_mul_lift_rank_of_isFractionRing_isLocalization R S FS M))
+
+end isFractionRing_isLocalization
+
+section field_isLocalization
+
+variable
+  (FS : Type*) [Field FS] [Algebra S FS]
+  [h : IsLocalization (algebraMapSubmonoid S R⁰) FS]
+  (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
+  (M₁ : Type v) [AddCommGroup M₁] [Module R M₁] [Module S M₁] [IsScalarTower R S M₁]
+include h
+
+/-- **Tower law over domains.**
+When `M` is a module over an algebra `S/R` of domains such that `(R⁰)⁻¹ S` is a field,
+we obtain a tower law.
+
+See `_root.lift_rank_mul_lift_rank` for when your modules are free.
+-/
+theorem lift_rank_mul_lift_rank_of_field_isLocalization :
+    lift.{w} (rank R S) * lift.{v} (rank S M) = lift.{v} (rank R M) :=
+  have : IsFractionRing S FS := .of_semifield_isLocalization (algebraMapSubmonoid S R⁰) _
+  lift_rank_mul_lift_rank_of_isFractionRing_isLocalization R S FS ..
+
+/-- **Tower law over domains.**
+When `M` is a module over an algebra `S/R` of domains such that `(R⁰)⁻¹ S` is a field,
+we obtain a tower law.
+
+See `_root.rank_mul_rank` for when your modules are free.
+-/
+theorem rank_mul_rank_of_field_isLocalization :
+    rank R S * rank S M₁ = rank R M₁ :=
+  have : IsFractionRing S FS := .of_semifield_isLocalization (algebraMapSubmonoid S R⁰) _
+  rank_mul_rank_of_isFractionRing_isLocalization R S FS ..
+
+/-- **Tower law over domains.**
+When `M` is a module over an algebra `S/R` of domains such that `(R⁰)⁻¹ S` is a field,
+we obtain a tower law.
+
+See `Module.finrank_mul_finrank` for when your modules are free.
+-/
+theorem finrank_mul_finrank_of_field_isLocalization :
+    finrank R S * finrank S M = finrank R M :=
+  have : IsFractionRing S FS := .of_semifield_isLocalization (algebraMapSubmonoid S R⁰) _
+  finrank_mul_finrank_of_isFractionRing_isLocalization R S FS ..
+
+end field_isLocalization
+
+variable (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
+
+/-- **Tower law for torsion-free modules.**
+The tower law for ENat `Module.rank` of a `S`-torsion-free module over an algebra `S/R` of domains.
+See `Module.IsTorsionFree.finrank_mul_finrank` for a `finrank` version.
+-/
+theorem IsTorsionFree.erank_mul_erank [IsTorsionFree S M] :
+    toENat (rank R S) * toENat (rank S M) = toENat (rank R M) := by
+  by_cases h : FaithfulSMul R S
+  case neg =>
+    have : ¬ FaithfulSMul R M := mt (·.tower_bot ..) h
+    simp [rank_eq_zero_of_not_faithfulSMul, h, this]
+  nontriviality R using subsingleton R S
+  have : NoZeroDivisors R := .of_faithfulSMul R S
+  have : Nontrivial S := FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective R S |>.nontrivial
+  have : IsDomain S := {}
+  nontriviality M using rank_subsingleton'
+  let FR := FractionRing R
+  let FS := Localization (algebraMapSubmonoid S R⁰)
+  have hFS := IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange R⁰ FR <| IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R S FS |>.toLinearMap
+  by_cases! hRS : rank R S < .aleph0
+  · have : Module.Finite FR FS := rank_lt_aleph0_iff.mp <| hFS.rank_eq ▸ hRS
+    have : IsDomain FS := IsLocalization.isDomain_localization <|
+      map_le_nonZeroDivisors_of_injective _ h.algebraMap_injective le_rfl
+    let : Field FS := fieldOfFiniteDimensional FR FS
+    simpa using congr($(lift_rank_mul_lift_rank_of_field_isLocalization R S FS M).toENat)
+  · rw [toENat_eq_top.mpr hRS, ENat.top_mul (by simpa using rank_pos.ne'), eq_comm, toENat_eq_top]
+    have ⟨m, hm⟩ := exists_ne (0 : M)
+    have hRSM := LinearMap.toSpanSingleton S M m |>.restrictScalars R
+      |>.lift_rank_le_of_injective <| smul_left_injective _ hm
+    exact aleph0_le_lift.mp <| .trans (aleph0_le_lift.mpr hRS) hRSM
+
+/-- **Tower law for torsion-free modules.**
+The tower law for `Module.finrank` of a `S`-torsion-free module over an algebra `S/R` of domains.
+See `Module.finrank_mul_finrank` for when your modules are free.
+-/
+theorem IsTorsionFree.finrank_mul_finrank [IsTorsionFree S M] :
+    finrank R S * finrank S M = finrank R M := by
+  simpa [finrank] using congr($(erank_mul_erank R S M).toNat)
+
+end Module
+
+namespace Algebra.IsAlgebraic
+
